cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3). He opens by singing praises to the LORD about His loving devotion and His justice. Then David starts making promises, friend, and I mean promise after promise after PROMISE.
First, David says he'll ponder the way that is blameless. Then, right in the middle of that thought, he stops and asks the LORD, "when will You come to me?"
Then David makes a big promise: he will walk with integrity of heart. And he names exactly where he's going to do it.

cards.question: Where does David say he'll walk with integrity of heart?

cards.text: Next, David makes a promise about his eyes: he'll set no worthless thing before them. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer staring at a takeout menu for a restaurant that closed, so I respect this man deeply.

cards.question: Then David talks about the work of those who fall away. What does he say about it?

answers.text: He hates it and it won't cling to him
He'll study it so he can learn from it
He'll leave it for someone else to judge

cards.text: Then David says a perverse heart shall depart from him. Not "step out for a minute." DEPART.

cards.question: Along with a perverse heart departing, David says he will know nothing of ___.

cards.text: Now David turns to the people around him, and some of them are about to have a VERY awkward meeting.

cards.question: What does David say he'll do to whoever slanders a neighbor in secret?
David says he'll put up with someone who has haughty eyes and a proud heart, as long as they keep quiet. True or false?

cards.text: But David isn't only showing people the door. His eyes are out looking for someone, like a boss scrolling résumés with a VERY short list of what he's hiring for.

cards.question: Who do David's eyes favor, so they may dwell with him?

answers.text: The wise men of the east

cards.question: And the person who walks in the way of integrity? David says they'll get to ___ to him.

cards.text: Then David gets to two kinds of people: the ones who practice deceit and the ones who tell lies. Both in the same verse. Somebody's about to find out where they stand.

cards.question: David says people who practice deceit can still dwell in his house, but people who tell lies can't stand in his presence. True or false?

cards.text: And David isn't saving this for someday. He puts it on a schedule, like a boss who books the meeting and then ACTUALLY shows up to it.

cards.question: When does David say he'll remove all the wicked of the land?
David says he'll cut off every evildoer from the city of the ___.

findings.problem: The blank in "the city of the ___" asks the baker to finish a line's wording rather than reason out its meaning. Nothing earlier sets up whose city it is. Also, "kings" is close enough to arguable, since Jerusalem is the king's city and David is the king speaking.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Send them to another land" could be argued as right. Psalm 101:8 says David will remove all the wicked of the land, and a secret slanderer fits that. A baker could read "remove" as sending them away.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
